payload.title: LeaveResolver.createLeaveRequest carries only @AuditLog while its self-service peers submit, cancel and update carry @UseGuards(RolesGuard, MobileFeatureGuard), @ModuleUserOrHigher() and @RequiresMobileFeature('leave'), so the per-user 'leave' mobile entitlement (SEC-HIGH-052) is not enforced server-side on creation and the explicit role contract is missing.
evidence: apps/hr-service/src/leave/leave.resolver.ts:526-530 (the submit comment says the contract matches createLeaveRequest, which it does not)
libs/backend-common/src/guards/mobile-feature.guard.ts:64-67 (a route with no @RequiresMobileFeature metadata makes the guard a no-op)
libs/backend-common/src/guards/roles.guard.ts:122-127 (a handler with no required roles admits any authenticated user)
payload.rule_violated: SEC-HIGH-052 (RESOLVED): the 'leave' mobile entitlement must be enforced server-side on every leave mutation, not only in the client; and the peer-boundary rule authz_boundary_missing_among_peers of the security-boundary adapter.
payload.notes: A tenant member whose auth.mobile_user_settings.allowedFeatures does not include 'leave' (an admin switched the feature off) calls createLeaveRequest with a crafted GraphQL request: no MobileFeatureGuard runs and the global RolesGuard admits any authenticated user, so the request is created, while submit, cancel and update refuse the same user. The body check limits it to the caller's own employee record, so the reach is narrower than the cross-employee case, but it is exactly the client-only-flag bypass SEC-HIGH-052 closed for the other three mutations. Close condition: Add @UseGuards(RolesGuard, MobileFeatureGuard), @ModuleUserOrHigher() and @RequiresMobileFeature('leave') to createLeaveRequest and add a resolver spec that reads ROLES_KEY and MOBILE_FEATURE_KEY metadata for all four self-service mutations; the security-boundary adapter hit on createLeaveRequest then disappears. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
